heterogeneous_mass_degradation.scientific_significance: Mass normalization (P/M) improves macro-average R2 across the whole cohort, but degrades RMSE in 7 of 18 subjects (light endurance and heavy athletes), demonstrating that simple linear allometry is insufficient and exhibits individual bias.

delta_efficiency_sensitivity_audit.scientific_rationale: The unlagged ramp regression slope beta1 = 0.00766 L/min/W yields an apparent delta efficiency of ~37.49% (NOT 25.5%). This value is an unlagged ramp regression parameter, not true steady-state delta efficiency. Pulmonary VO2 lags cellular respiration by ~35-45s, and during continuous ramp testing to exhaustion, steady state is never attained. True delta efficiency requires constant-load multi-stage steady states, which are absent in ACTES.

identified_parameters.notes: Unlagged ramp regression slope beta1 = Delta VO2 / Delta P = 0.00766 L/min/W. Apparent ramp delta efficiency eta_delta = 1 / (beta1 * 348.33) is ~37.49% (NOT 25.5%). Because pulmonary VO2 lags cellular respiration and ACTES lacks constant-load steady states, true physiological delta efficiency is NOT IDENTIFIABLE.
Gross efficiency starts at 0% at rest (P=0, VO2>0) and rises non-linearly with workload. Cannot be equated to regression slope beta1.
Nested subject-level cross-validation without test leakage confirms optimal generalization at tau = 35.0 s across folds.
Linear mass scaling (exponent gamma = 1.0) improves macro-average R2 from 0.6059 to 0.7371, but degrades RMSE in 7/18 subjects, indicating non-linear or multi-component allometry.

strictly_unidentifiable_parameters.reason: ACTES provides pulmonary breath exchange, not in-bore localized 31P-MRS.
No magnetic resonance chemical shift or muscle biopsy available.
No high-density surface EMG or needle EMG recorded in ACTES.
No 3D MRI segmentation available (Franke 2020 single-subject anchor remains un-cross-validated).
ACTES protocol is graded incremental test to exhaustion (~15 min), not 45-min constant extreme stress.
